Definition: (causative) to bone, i.e. denude (by extensive, craunch) the bones
BiblicalUsage: Garam means to strip the bones, to gnaw them bare. God says Israel shall eat up the nations, break their bones, and pierce them with arrows, in Numbers 24:8. The princes of Jerusalem are evening wolves who gnaw not the bones till the morrow in Zephaniah 3:3, and the unfaithful woman must break the sherds and pluck off her own breasts in Ezekiel 23:34.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the stripped bone is the picture of judgment without mercy. The wolves gnaw all night and leave nothing, and I hold that the God who breaks bones can also set them, if we turn to Him.
